added_lemmas.gap: The fixed-\(\mu>1\) interior theorem has order \(\sigma\sqrt n\), but it does not cover the active boundary \(\mu=1\); the boundary instead has order \(\sigma\) for a nondegenerate level interval and zero radius for a known singleton level.

obligation.what_is_open: Characterize separately the shrinking-incoherence boundary layer and the fixed-interior arbitrary multi-chart wedge frontier, with matching honest upper and all-procedure lower bounds when possible.
obligation.obstruction: The boundary proof uses discrete sign recovery once incoherence is exactly active, whereas the interior proof uses continuous perturbations with slack. Neither argument is uniform as the slack vanishes, and no same-class tangent packing is available for every admissible multi-chart wedge.
obligation.attempted: The exact \(\mu=1\) reduction and the fixed-\(\mu>1\) one-block frontier determine the two endpoint regimes, but they do not determine an interpolation scale or control chart synchronization and mask amplification uniformly over general wedges.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper indexes the Gaussian panel experiment by admissible tuples \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\), so the latent counterfactual matrix remains part of the experiment index even when tuples induce the same observed law. The balanced rank-one L-mask has a sharp phase split. For each fixed \(\mu>1\), Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} gives the all-procedure and polynomial-time frontier \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\sqrt n\). At the saturated boundary \(\mu=1\), both normalized overlap Grams equal one for every \(0<\kappa\le1\): Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} proves \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\) when \(s_-<s_+\), but \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}=0\) when the common level \(s_-=s_+\) is known. The unrestricted tangent modulus nevertheless remains at least \(\sigma\sqrt{2n}\), so it cannot support a uniform same-class lower comparison at the boundary. Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge} separates the shrinking-incoherence layer from the arbitrary interior multi-chart wedge frontier without asserting an interpolation rate. The diffuse-weight ATT interval remains only a coverage-valid nuclear/operator-duality corollary.

project_justification.gap: Sharp staggered-panel inference is usually coordinatewise or functional-specific, while global matrix confidence theory typically uses random or isotropic measurements. No located result gives a tuple-indexed honest nuclear ball under a deterministic adoption wedge together with both the fixed-interior frontier and the saturated-incoherence boundary elbow. Yan and Wainwright's two-potential-outcome-matrix class uses two-sided subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise, and target-local leverage conditions rather than this note's global incoherence class, so only a converse can transfer upward from an embedded subclass; their construction does not establish the present upper bounds.
project_justification.niche: Known rank, independent Gaussian cells, strong factors, and quantitative overlap Grams isolate a deterministic-wedge confidence problem with a genuine boundary phase change. In the balanced rank-one L-mask, fixed \(\mu>1\) permits continuous factor perturbations and a \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier, whereas \(\mu=1\) fixes all singular-vector magnitudes, makes overlap automatically exact for every \(\kappa\le1\), and leaves only signs and the factor level to learn.
project_justification.fill: Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} retains the fixed-\(\mu>1\) \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier and its total polynomial-time spectral certificate. Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} gives the full \(\mu=1\) boundary frontier: an explicit polynomial-time honest radius of order \(\sigma\), a fixed-sign two-level all-procedure lower bound when \(s_-<s_+\), exact zero radius when the common level is known, and the simultaneous lower bound \(\mathfrak R_n\ge\sigma\sqrt{2n}\). Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge} leaves only the shrinking-incoherence layer and the arbitrary interior multi-chart frontier open.

sampling_model.design: The schedule \(g_n\), wedge \(\Omega_n\), dimensions, rank, noise variance, and class constants are fixed and known. The fixed-\(\mu>1\) rate-optimal spectral theorem and the separate \(\mu=1\) sign-based boundary theorem are both restricted to the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask.
sampling_model.overlap: The full class imposes quantitative observed-subblock Grams. In the unique balanced chart at \(\mu=1\), every singular-vector coordinate has squared magnitude \(1/n\), so both normalized overlap Grams equal one and every \(0<\kappa\le1\) defines the same boundary class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For fixed \(\mu>1\), the total spectral procedure uses independent Gaussian pilot and inference copies, total pseudoinverse conventions, one-step block transport, an ordered conditional Gaussian nuclear quantile, a homogeneous observable remainder, and a deterministic fallback; its \(\sigma\sqrt n\) guarantee is not asserted at \(\mu=1\). At \(\mu=1\), a separate deterministic \(O(n^2)\) procedure recovers row and column relative signs exponentially accurately, estimates the unknown level by a signed average when \(s_-<s_+\), and uses the known level with zero radius when \(s_-=s_+\).

prose_updates.related_work: Yan and Wainwright provide the closest computational and inferential comparison, but their model has two low-rank potential-outcome matrices, two-sided observed-subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise and target-local leverage conditions, and no global incoherence condition. Their class is therefore not identical to \(\Theta_n\): only the converse transfers upward through an embedded subclass, while the present constructive nuclear-radius bounds remain specific to this note's class. Bai and Ng supply tall-wide factor-rotation expansions under strong observed subblocks. Carpentier and Nickl study honest nuclear confidence diameter in isotropic Gaussian trace regression, where rank adaptation is the central obstruction. Capponi and Stojnic analyze worst-case Frobenius residuals for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block. Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan treat debiased uncertainty quantification under random sampling, and Chatterjee gives qualitative recoverability under arbitrary deterministic masks. Against these comparators, Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} supplies the fixed-\(\mu>1\) interior \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier, while Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} proves the \(\mu=1\), arbitrary-\(\kappa\) \(\sigma\)-or-zero boundary frontier and the failure of the unrestricted tangent-modulus lower comparison. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright and Farias, Li, and Peng remain functional-specific benchmarks; the ATT proposition claims coverage transfer and no optimal-length comparison.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The \(\sigma\sqrt n\) certificate and packing theorem remain confined to fixed \(\mu>1\) in the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask. The new boundary proof is also benchmark-specific: it uses the exact \(\mu=1\) reduction to equal-magnitude singular vectors and the resulting rank-one sign experiment. It neither supplies a rate uniform over \(\mu=\mu(n)\downarrow1\) nor controls arbitrary connected multi-chart wedges. A broader result would need a uniform post-synchronization envelope and nuclear-mask amplification bound together with a same-class packing that preserves exact rank, strong factors, incoherence, overlap, and controlled observed-law divergence. Those are the two separate tasks in Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge}; no interpolation exponent is currently claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The fixed-\(\mu>1\) balanced rank-one two-sided frontier, the full \(\mu=1\) boundary characterization, the total one-block spectral certificate, and the diffuse-weight ATT coverage corollary are theorem results. At the boundary, arbitrary \(0<\kappa\le1\) is covered because both normalized Grams equal one; the minimax radius is of order \(\sigma\) for \(s_-<s_+\) and exactly zero for the known singleton level \(s_-=s_+\). Neither theorem covers the shrinking-incoherence layer or arbitrary interior multi-chart wedges; those are stated separately in Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge}. No theorem is asserted for unknown rank, approximate low rank, dependent or heteroskedastic errors, adaptive adoption, or optimal ATT length. In the noiseless one-chart case, the supporting block-transport lemma reduces to exact tall-wide transport.
